title: Everything a rhYgtaSA user would otherwise download by hand
readme: rhY's rule: anything a user would fetch by hand is hosted by us (https mirror + torrent), so the
install stays 'downgrade to 1.0 US, run the installer'. This file is the single source of truth for
what to host: name, size, sha256, source page, author, licence, where it goes in the game folder,
and the urls. tools/fetch-deps.sh reads it; tests/test_fetch_deps.py validates it.
sha256 'TBD' means we do not have the file yet - fetch-deps.sh then refuses to install it (an
unverified archive must not reach a game folder). A url 'TBD' means no host yet: the entry is
reported as a manual download from source_page and is not counted as a failure.
redistribute: 'no' entries keep mirror/torrent at TBD on purpose - docs/CHARACTERS.md section 9
records that MixMods forbids re-upload ('share the same download link') and that the two LibertyCity
Peds Vary packs answer No to re-upload and 'under no circumstances' to using the assets. Hosting them
needs written permission from the authors first; that is tracked here, not in a chat log.
name is OUR hosted file name (stable, ascii). upstream_name is the author's own file name and is TBD
until someone writes down what the download button actually served.
The bundle: tools/make-release.sh OUTDIR collects every entry whose file is staged in vendor/ (or
--stage DIR), writes SHA256SUMS, makes ONE torrent for the whole folder with the trackers in
deps/trackers.txt, re-derives the info hash from the bytes on disk before printing the magnet, and
--update-manifest writes sha256/size/magnet back into this file. Only redistribute: yes entries are
collected by default; ask/no need --include-ask/--include-no plus --permission-note (docs/CHARACTERS.md
section 9). A magnet slot that is still TBD means the file is not staged yet, not that we may not host it.

hosts.torrent_tracker: deps/trackers.txt (public announce URLs, one per line, no comments; the three listed answered a UDP connect on 2026-11-11)
hosts.bundle: rhygtasa-deps-<version>/ - one folder of archives + SHA256SUMS + manifest.json + README.txt, one torrent for the whole folder, built by tools/make-release.sh (build/release is the intended OUTDIR)
hosts.magnet: TBD: no archive is staged yet (vendor/ does not exist), so no torrent exists yet to point at. tools/make-release.sh --update-manifest fills the magnet slot of every entry it collects.
hosts.note: when rhY's https host exists, mirror url = mirror_base + '/' + name. Until then the magnet is the only thing that exists, and only for entries the licence allows: redistribute yes by default, ask/no only with a written permission note. GTASA-Remix is ~10 GB (GitHub reports 10329625 KB for the repo), which is exactly why the transport is a torrent and not a download button.

files.license: NVIDIA RTX Remix License (EULA accepted at download)
files.notes: replaces the pack's runtime: d3d9.dll + .trex/ in the game folder (README install step 2). The source url is the real asset URL, HEAD-checked 200 on 2026-11-11; it redirects to a signed release-assets.githubusercontent.com URL that expires, so keep the /releases/download/ form. redistribute 'ask': check the Remix licence before mirroring.

files.name: TBD
files.author: Tomasak (downgraders), ICan'tReadYourMind (installer)
files.license: closed-source freeware archive; the author's site is the only download we use - ask before mirroring
files.notes: step 1 of the two-step install: Steam 3.0 -> 1.0 US. This is the tool docs/notes/linux-modding-notes.md describes: 'RGSC/Steam to v1' for SA = install.bat + jptch.exe + SA DOWNGRADE/*.diff, run under plain Wine (DISPLAY= wine jptch.exe <old> 'SA DOWNGRADE/<NAME>.diff' <old>.down); it yields the 1.0 US compact exe 5,189,632 B, main.scm 3,079,599, script.img 581,632. GTASA-Remix's own README links the same site, whose page credits 'Tomasak - Downgraders'. curl -sI checked 200 (the http form 301s) on 2026-11-12. Native-Linux alternative, MIT, checked 200: https://github.com/xxanqw/gtasa-open-downgrader (NewSteam R2 -> v1.0 US Hoodlum, AppImage, its own 4GB/LAA switch). sha256 stays TBD: the site publishes no hash, so fetch-deps.sh must never install these bytes unverified. Its exe is not Large Address Aware, which is why apply.sh sets the flag (tools/laa.py, docs/VEGETATION.md cause 2).
